fieldDocs.exampleInfo: Information: the information icon and the help text.

switchDocs.summary: A switch that turns a setting on or off, with an immediate effect. The position of the knob shows the state: left, off; right, on. The label sits after the track, and the piece fires the native input and change when the person toggles it.
switchDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-switch spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P79. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: For a setting that turns on or off, with an immediate effect, outside a toolbar.
Several settings stack, one nph-switch per line: there is no group component.
Without text only when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell, always with label.
whenNotToUse: In a form, when the choice only counts on submission: use nph-checkbox.
In a toolbar, among other buttons: use nph-togglebutton.
To paint the track or the knob by hand: use checked, invalid and disabled.
To hide the label by deleting its text: leave text empty and give label.
switchDocs.relationsText: In a toolbar, among other buttons, the piece is nph-togglebutton; in a form whose choice only counts on submission, it is nph-checkbox. The piece brings its own text: it does not need nph-field to have a name. Inside nph-field, it is one option of a group.
api: The on state, the Figma property marcado. false by default. Reflected to the attribute. A click, Enter or Space by the person toggles it and fires input and change; setting it from code fires nothing.

The label, already localized, after the track. It is the accessible name and wraps to the available width. Without it (the Figma boolean that shows the label, off), the piece is only the track and needs label.
Accessible name of the piece without text. Required there; with text, it is not used.

The track outline becomes status/error, on or off, and on focus the halo becomes focus/halo-error. Reflected to the attribute; it sets aria-invalid. The error sentence stays outside the piece. disabled wins over it.

Turns the piece off: it leaves the Tab order, does not toggle, fires nothing and stays at state/disabled-opacity. Reflected to the attribute. A disabled fieldset around it does the same, except inside its first legend.
The native events, fired in this order when the person toggles the piece. input bubbles and crosses shadow roots; change bubbles and does not. The new value is read from event.target.checked.
states: The track is color/input, with no outline; the knob is color/background, on the left.
The track is color/primary, with an outline in color/primary-border drawn inside it; the knob is color/primary-foreground, on the right.
Over the whole piece, the fill goes to color/input-hover when off and color/primary-hover when on; the outline stays.
For keyboard users: the track outline turns focus/border and a halo in focus/halo shows outside the track, both fully rounded, without changing the size.
The track outline is status/error, on or off; on focus, the halo is focus/halo-error. The error sentence stays outside the piece.
The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order; on keeps its outline. It wins over invalid: the error outline is not drawn.
switchDocs.statesCaption: off, on, invalid, disabled and disabled with invalid. Move the mouse over a piece to see hover and press Tab to see focus.
switchDocs.labelText: The label sits after the track, space/inline from it, in text/label-md and color/foreground. It wraps to the available width; with two lines, the track sits at the top, aligned with the first line. Without text the piece is only the track, and label gives it a name.
switchDocs.labelCaption: With a label, only the track with label, and a long label on two lines.
anatomy: The rounded base, radius/full, switch/track-width by icon/size-lg. Off: color/input, no outline. On: color/primary, with an outline border/width in color/primary-border drawn inside. Hover: color/input-hover or color/primary-hover. Invalid: outline status/error.
The circle in icon/size-sm, space/inline-tight from the track edge. Off: on the left, in color/background. On: on the right, in color/primary-foreground. It slides by transform.
The text after the track, in text/label-md and color/foreground, space/inline from the track. It is the name of the control.
The whole track, switch/track-width by icon/size-lg; with a label, the whole piece.
The track outline turns focus/border and a halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo shows outside the track, both radius/full; with an error, status/error and focus/halo-error.
accessibility: Semantics
A native button with type=button, role=switch and aria-checked following checked; the track is aria-hidden. invalid sets aria-invalid. The piece is not associated with a form.
Accessible name
The label text. Without text, label is required and becomes the aria-label of the button.
Keyboard
Tab enters and leaves; Space and Enter toggle.
Visible focus
Keyboard only: the focus outline and the halo around the track, without changing the size.
Contrast

The track edge passes 3:1 on the page background: color/input is 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark; color/primary-border is at least 4.96:1 in light and 4.91:1 in dark, in every brand. The knob passes 3:1 on its track: color/background on color/input is 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark; color/primary-foreground on color/primary is at least 4.96:1. The error outline, status/error, is 6.88:1 in light and 5.01:1 in dark.
Known limit

focus/border against focus/halo is below 3:1 only in the default brand in light mode, at 2.92:1, as design.md records; in every other brand and scheme it passes. A forced-colors mode and a right-to-left page are not handled yet. The error sentence outside the piece cannot be tied to it by aria-describedby across the shadow root.
Color is not the only signal
On and off show in the knob position, not only in the track color. The error has its sentence written outside the piece.
Touch target
The whole track, 40 by 24 px; with a label, the whole piece.
Motion

The knob slides and the colors change on motion/state-duration and motion/state-easing. Under reduced motion the knob does not slide: it changes side by opacity, on motion/hover-duration, and the color still changes.

sliderDocs.summary: The control that picks a value, or a range, on a continuous scale of numbers, by dragging a thumb or with the arrow keys. It takes part in the form that contains it; the help and the error message belong to nph-field.
sliderDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-slider spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P94. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
sliderDocs.description: Use nph-slider when the position on the scale matters more than the exact number: volume, brightness, a price range. When the exact number matters, turn on inputs or use nph-input. It does not show progress: that is a progress bar, which is not operated.
whenToUse: single, to pick an approximate value on a scale, such as volume or brightness.
range, to filter by a range, such as a minimum and a maximum price.
vertical, in a narrow panel or for a setting that goes up and down, such as volume or zoom.
text, outside nph-field, when the person needs to see the number while adjusting.
limits, when the ends of the scale are not obvious to the person.
marks, when only some values are valid, in fixed steps.
inputs, when the exact number matters and the person may want to type it.
steppers, when fine adjustment is common or dragging is hard, as on a touch screen.
Inside nph-field when the value breaks a rule: the field gives the error message.
whenNotToUse: To show progress: that is a progress bar, which is not operated.
range to pick a single value: use single.
vertical in a common form: the horizontal one follows the reading.
text inside nph-field: the label comes out twice.
limits together with marks: the marks already show the ends.
marks on a continuous scale: use limits.
Alone when the person often types exact numbers: turn on inputs or use nph-input.
steppers without a defined step: each click needs to move one clear step.
sliderDocs.relationsText: nph-field gives the label, the help and the error message, and writes label, description, invalid and required on the slider; text stays off there. On its own, nph-label names it with for, or text draws the label above the track. The value balloon is nph-tooltip, the field is nph-input and minus and plus are icon-only nph-button.
api: horizontal (default) or vertical. The vertical one has the minimum at the bottom, and only text and limits exist in it. Reflected to the attribute.
single (default), one thumb, or range, two thumbs, start and end. Reflected to the attribute.
The scale: 0, 100 and 1 by default. Every value is rounded to the step and kept inside the scale.

The current value, in single. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(); it applies only until the person moves the slider. Setting it from code fires no event. Its default is the middle of the scale.
The start and the end, in range, with the same rule as value. Each thumb stops at the other. By default, min and max.
The name of the entry in the form data: single submits name=value, range two entries under the same name, start and end. Reflected to the attribute.
The visible label, drawn by an nph-label with the current value beside it, above the track. Empty turns the part off. Off inside nph-field.
Turns on the minimum and the maximum at the ends of the track.
Turns on one label per step under the track, at most 100. Horizontal only.
Turns on an nph-input with the number: one at the end in single, one at each end in range. Horizontal only.
Turns on the minus and plus buttons, which move one step. Horizontal only; requires decrease-label and increase-label.
In range, the accessible name of each thumb and of its field, already localized.
The accessible names of the minus and plus buttons, already localized.
The accessible name in text, never visible, when no label is associated. An associated label wins over it, and it wins over text.
The accessible description in text, never visible: the help or the error sentence that nph-field writes. Read as the description of each thumb.
Written by nph-field. A slider always has a value, so it has no effect.
The whole slider at state/disabled-opacity, once, out of the Tab order and of the form data. A disabled fieldset disables it too. It wins over invalid.
The erro state: the thumb border becomes status/error and each thumb gets aria-invalid. The sentence belongs to nph-field.
The native events. input fires while the value moves; change when it settles: after a key or a click, and on the release of a drag. Read the value from the host.
variants: General use, following the reading. The minimum is on the left.
A narrow panel, or a setting that goes up and down, such as volume or zoom. The minimum is at the bottom.
One approximate value on the scale, such as volume or brightness.
A start and an end, such as a minimum and a maximum price. Each thumb has a name of its own.
sliderDocs.variantsCaption: single and range, horizontal and vertical.
states: The thumb on color/background, with the color/primary-border border. The track is color/input empty and color/primary active.
The value balloon, an nph-tooltip, opens above the thumb.
The thumb border becomes focus/border, with the halo focus/halo outside, at focus/ring-width. The balloon opens.
The thumb border is status/error; with focus, the halo is focus/halo-error. The inner fields show their error.
The whole slider at state/disabled-opacity, once; no balloon. The field and the buttons keep their resting look. It wins over invalid.
sliderDocs.statesCaption: Default, invalid and disabled. Move the mouse over a thumb to see the balloon, and press Tab to see focus.
sliderDocs.partsText: Each part is turned on by a property and does not create a variant. The parts beside the track sit at space/inline from it.
parts: The nph-label and the current value above the track.
The minimum and the maximum at the ends, in text/caption.
One label per step under the track, in text/caption. Horizontal only.
An nph-input with the number; in range, one at each end. Horizontal only.
Icon-only nph-button, secondary and ghost, with minus and plus. Each click moves one step. Horizontal only.
sliderDocs.invalidText: An orientation or a mode outside its values, a min that is not below max and a step that is not a positive number draw nothing. marks, inputs or steppers in the vertical orientation, and steppers without its two names, are not drawn; the rest renders.
anatomy: A vertical stack, space/stack-tight between the top line, the track and the marks. Default width layout/input-width.
Empty part in color/input and active part in color/primary, space/inline-tight thick, radius/full. In range, the active part sits between the two thumbs.
A circle of icon/size-sm, radius/full, color/background, with the border/width border inside in color/primary-border. Its touch target is a circle of control/height-large centered on it.
An nph-tooltip above the thumb, with the tooltip tokens. In range, it follows the thumb that has the state.
The nph-label on the left and the value on the right, in text/label-md, color/foreground.
text/caption, color/muted-foreground. The marks sit space/stack-tight below the track.
nph-input in size=default, and icon-only nph-button, space/inline from the track.
accessibility: Semantics

Each thumb is an element with role=slider, with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext and aria-orientation. In range, an inner group holds the two thumbs. The host is form-associated and labelable.
Accessible name

From the label associated with the host: nph-label for, a label element or nph-field. Without one, from label, then from text. In range, each thumb takes start-label or end-label; minus and plus take decrease-label and increase-label.
Description
description is read as the description of each thumb: the help or the error sentence of nph-field.
Keyboard
Tab enters each thumb. The arrows move one step; Page Up and Page Down a tenth of the scale; Home and End go to the ends.
Visible focus
The thumb takes focus/border with the halo outside, without changing the size, and the balloon opens.
Touch target
The thumb is drawn at icon/size-sm, and its target is a circle of control/height-large.
Known limits

selectDocs.summary: The field that opens a closed list of options for the person to pick one. It takes part in the form that contains it; the label, the help and the error message belong to nph-field.
selectDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-select and nph-option spec sheets, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P91. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
selectDocs.sourceOption: Figma, nph-select / opção (1357:136); nph-option spec sheet
selectDocs.sourceDecisions: Task DSA-29, answers D1 to D9; docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md › P91

selectDocs.description: Use nph-select when the person picks a single option from a closed list of 6 to 15 items. It does not replace nph-radio, for 2 to 5 options visible at once, nor nph-combobox, for more than 15 options or when the person needs to search. To pick several options, use nph-multi-combobox.
whenToUse: When the person picks a single option from a closed list of 6 to 15 items.
Inside an nph-field, which gives the label, the help text and the error message.
With start=avatar when the options are people, and start=icon when a symbol helps recognize the option.
default in general use; large on the screen that needs the 44 px target, for every field of the form.
whenNotToUse: For 2 to 5 options: use nph-radio, so the person sees all of them without opening anything.
For more than 15 options, or when the person needs to search: use nph-combobox.
To pick several options: use nph-multi-combobox.
To name the field with the placeholder alone: it is replaced by the choice.
With the magnifying glass at the start: search belongs to nph-combobox.
selectDocs.relationsText: The options are nph-option children, as option children of a select; the list is internal. nph-field composes the label, the select, the help and the error message, and writes label, description, invalid and required on the select. The start avatar is an nph-avatar; the start icon, the arrow and the check are nph-icon instances.
api: default or large, reflected. The height of the trigger and the width of the arrow area change.

The current value. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(). The chosen option is the first nph-option with that value; the value is kept until such an option arrives. Setting it from code fires nothing.
The invitation before a choice, already localized, such as Select an option. It is not a name.
none, icon or avatar. The trigger repeats the start of the chosen option; before a choice, the icon property or the empty avatar. The dot of an option never goes to the trigger.
A core name of nph-icon, default globe: the start icon before a choice, or when the chosen option has no icon. Not the magnifying glass.
Boolean, reflected. The list is open. The piece opens and closes it; the consumer may set it. Opening and closing fire no event.
As in a native field. With no chosen option, the entry is left out of the form data; required with no choice is valueMissing, with the message of the browser.
The erro state: the border becomes status/error and the trigger gets aria-invalid. The sentence belongs to nph-field.
Boolean, reflected. The whole piece fades, leaves the Tab order and the form data, and the list does not open. A disabled fieldset disables it too.
The accessible name and description in text, never visible, written by nph-field. An associated label wins over label.
Fired by the host, in this order, when the person chooses an option of a different value. Code fires neither.
selectDocs.invalidText: A size outside default and large, a start outside none, icon and avatar, or an icon outside the core: the select does not render and emits console.error in development. The magnifying glass renders and warns: search belongs to nph-combobox.
selectDocs.sizesText: default in general use; large on the screen that needs the 44 px target, for every field of the form. The height of the trigger and the width of the arrow area change: control/height-default or control/height-large.
selectDocs.sizesCaption: default and large, with a chosen option.
states: Border color/input on color/background; the arrow area in color/accent, after a color/border divider.
Keyboard focus: border focus/border and the focus/halo outside, at focus/radius-control.
The focus look with the list open below the trigger and the arrow up.
Border status/error, also on hover; with focus, the halo is focus/halo-error.
color/muted, border color/input and state/disabled-opacity on the whole piece; it wins over the error.
selectDocs.startText: start decides the kind and the chosen option gives the art: with icon, the icon of the chosen option, or globe before a choice; with avatar, the photo of the chosen person, or the empty avatar before a choice. Keep the same start on every option of the list.
selectDocs.startCaption: start=icon and start=avatar, before and after a choice.
selectDocs.optionText: Each option is an nph-option: its label is the text it holds, and it may have a start, a secondary text and the dot of a state. The list writes selected and active on it; the selected option has the color/primary-surface background and the check, which win over the hover look.
selectDocs.optionCaption: The four starts, active, selected, the dot in every state and disabled.
optionApi: The label, already localized: the accessible name of the option and the text of the trigger when it is chosen.
Reflected. Without the attribute, the label text.
The helper text after the label. Empty turns it off.
The icon with start=icon, default globe; the photo with start=avatar, empty for the empty avatar.
The dot with start=dot: neutral, info, warning, success, error or help. Absent, the text color.
Boolean, reflected. The option fades and cannot be chosen.
check (default) or checkbox, reflected. nph-select always uses check; checkbox is the multiple choice of nph-multi-combobox (P96).
Written by the list, never by the consumer. Not reflected.
optionStates: The label in color/popover-foreground, with no background.
color/accent with the text in color/accent-foreground.
color/primary-surface and the check in color/primary; it wins over hover.
selectDocs.listText: The list opens space/inline-tight below the trigger, with its width, and turns up when it does not fit below. It fades in and slides into place; with reduced motion, only the opacity changes. It shows 8 whole options inside layout/max-list-height and scrolls above that. The focus stays on the trigger, which points to the active option.
selectDocs.listCaption: The open list, the chosen option with the check.
keyboard: Closed: open the list on the chosen option, or on the first one.
Open on, or move to, the first and the last option.
Open: move the active option, without wrapping.
Move to the option that starts with the typed text; closed, they open the list.
Open: choose the active option and close.
Close without choosing; the focus moves on.
anatomy: Background color/background, border border/width in color/input, radius/control, width layout/input-width, height control/height-*, left padding space/control-padding, gap space/inline, right padding 0.
nph-icon icon/size-sm in color/muted-foreground, or nph-avatar sm.
The chosen value in text/body-md, color/foreground; the placeholder in color/muted-foreground. One line with an ellipsis.
border/width in color/border, beside the arrow area.
color/accent, control/height-* wide and the trigger height minus its borders; radius/none on the left and radius/control-inner on the right; chevron-down, or chevron-up open.
color/popover, border color/input, radius/container, padding space/inline-tight, maximum height layout/max-list-height, elevation/dropdown.
Padding and gap space/inline, radius/inner, the width of the list; start icon, avatar or dot.
nph-icon check, icon/size-sm, color/primary, at the end of the selected option.
accessibility: Semantics
A select-only combobox: the trigger has role combobox and controls a listbox; each nph-option has role option and aria-selected.
Accessible name
The label of nph-field, or label; the placeholder is not a name. description is read with it: the help or the error sentence.
Keyboard and focus
The focus stays on the trigger and points to the active option with aria-activedescendant. The focus shows for the keyboard and while the list is open.
Contrast
Text 4.5:1 and the border 3:1, in light and dark mode; the arrow 3:1 on color/accent; the check 4.78:1 and 6.26:1 on color/primary-surface.
Color is not the only signal
The error comes as text in nph-field; the selected option has the check; the dot goes with the written state; the arrow turns up when the list opens.
Hidden parts
The start, the divider, the arrow, the dot and the check are hidden from the screen reader.

inputOtpDocs.summary: A short code field, one cell per character, to confirm access with a code sent by SMS or e-mail. One native input lies over the cells, so the code is one value with one name; the label, the help and the error come from nph-field.
inputOtpDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-input-otp spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P85. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To confirm access with a code sent by SMS or e-mail: length 6 or 4, by the length of the code.
On a touch screen, where the code is usually typed on the phone: size large; on other screens, size default.
When the code is typed in a public place: masked.
For a code with letters and numbers, such as A7K2Q9: the field takes it and the cell does not change.
whenNotToUse: For free one-line text: use nph-input.
Without nph-field: the label, the help and the error belong to nph-field.
With cells of different sizes: use the same size in the whole field.
To paint the resend action with a loose color: the resend is an nph-button below the field, with the label in color/link.
inputOtpDocs.relationsText: nph-field carries the label, the help and the error, and writes label, description, invalid and required on the field. The resend action is an nph-button below the field, disabled during the countdown: it is not part of the field. For free one-line text, use nph-input.
api: 6 (default) or 4: the number of cells. Any other value draws nothing.
default (36 px) or large (44 px), the same in every cell. large is for a touch screen.
Error border on every cell and aria-invalid. The error sentence belongs to nph-field. disabled wins.
Out of the Tab order, muted background and lower opacity. A disabled fieldset does the same.
A dot in place of each character, for a code typed in a public place. Visual only: a screen reader reads the code.
Announced as aria-required. There is no constraint validation.
The name of the entry in the form data. It reflects, because the form reads the attribute.
The code: letters and digits only, up to length. The attribute is the initial and reset value; the property is the current one. Setting it from code fires nothing.
The accessible name, as text, when no label is associated with the field. nph-field writes it.
The accessible description, as text: the help or the error sentence that nph-field writes.
Native events. input crosses the shadow root once per change the person makes; the host fires change when the person leaves the field or presses Enter with a new value.
inputOtpDocs.sizeText: length sets the number of cells by the length of the code. size sets the side of every cell: default on most screens, large on a touch screen, where the code is usually typed on the phone. The cells of one field always share the size.
inputOtpDocs.sizeCaption: Six cells in default and in large; four cells in default.
inputOtpDocs.statesText: The state of the field applies to every cell. Hover darkens every border, because the field is one target; focus marks only the active cell, where the next character goes.
statesRules: Every border color/input-hover. Error and disabled keep their border.
The active cell takes the focus/border and the focus/halo outside it, out of the layout.
Every border status/error; with focus, the halo is focus/halo-error.
Background color/muted and state/disabled-opacity; it wins over invalid.
inputOtpDocs.maskedText: masked shows a dot in place of each character, for a code typed in a public place. Elsewhere, seeing the character helps the person check it. The field takes letters and numbers in both cases, and the cell does not change.
inputOtpDocs.maskedCaption: A code with letters and numbers, and the same code masked.
anatomy: The row of cells, one per character, space/inline apart, with the native input laid over it.
A square of control/height-default or control/height-large, with no inner padding: background color/background, border color/input at border/width, radius radius/control.
text/code in color/foreground: a letter or a digit.
In place of the character when masked, in text/code and color/foreground.
A ring outside the active cell, focus/ring-width wide. It takes no space.
accessibility: Semantics
One native text input with autocomplete one-time-code. The cells only draw and are hidden from assistive technology: the code is one value, with one name.
Accessible name
The label of nph-field, written as label. A label associated with the field names it first. With no name, the field renders and warns in development.
Description
The help or the error sentence of nph-field, written as description, read with the name.
Keyboard
One Tab stop for the whole code. Typing fills the active cell; Backspace removes the character before the caret; the arrows, Home and End move the active cell; Enter submits the form.
Visible focus
The active cell shows the focus border and the halo; the space between cells is wider than the halo.
Contrast
The character and the dot are at least 4.5:1, and the border at least 3:1, in light and dark in every brand. Disabled has no minimum.
Color is not the only signal
The error always comes with the sentence of nph-field; disabled combines opacity with the muted background.
Touch target
The whole field is the target. Each cell is 36 px in default and 44 px in large; on a touch screen, use large.
Known limits

masked is visual only: a screen reader reads the code. The input uses text/code, 14 px, so iOS Safari may zoom on focus. That iOS offers a code received by SMS to this field is to be confirmed on a device.

dialogDocs.summary: Modal window that blocks the page until the person finishes or cancels a short task, always over the overlay/scrim veil.
dialogDocs.matrixLabel: nph-dialog by size and by actions
dialogDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-dialog spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P87. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
dialogDocs.description: Use nph-dialog for a short task that needs the full attention of the person before going on: edit a record, fill in a short form, choose an option. To confirm a destructive action, such as deleting or discarding, use nph-alert-dialog. A long flow goes to a page, and a notice that asks for no answer does not use a dialog.
whenToUse: A short task that needs an answer before going on: edit a record, fill in a short form, choose an option.
Choose the size by the content, as the width ceiling: sm for a choice or a short confirmation without a destructive action, md for a short form, lg for a table, a long list or a two-column form.
Turn on the lines with long content, such as a list or a table.
Use stacked actions on a narrow screen.
whenNotToUse: To confirm a destructive action, such as deleting or discarding: use nph-alert-dialog.
For a long flow: it goes to a page.
For a notice that asks for no answer: use a message on the page itself.
To open a dialog over another: finish or close the first one.
api: The title, already localized by the application: the task or the question. It names the dialog for the screen reader. Required: without it, nothing is drawn.
The support sentence below the title, which completes the name. Empty: no description.
sm, md (default) or lg: the width ceiling. The dialog hugs its content from layout/dialog-min-width up to the ceiling.
inline (default) or stacked. stacked puts the footer buttons one per line, the primary on top, below the md breakpoint.
Turns off the close button. Turn it off only when the footer already offers the way out; Esc still closes the dialog.
The accessible name of the close button, already localized. Required while the button is shown.
The line between the header and the content, for long content.
The line between the content and the footer, for long content. Drawn only when the footer has buttons.
Boolean, reflected. The only way to open and close the dialog; it turns false by itself when the person closes it.
The content area: fields, text, a list. Its width sets the width of the dialog. Empty, the area is not drawn. It is the only part that scrolls.
The nph-button actions: the solid secondary first, the primary or the danger last. Empty, the footer is not drawn.
Fired before the dialog closes when the person asks, with Esc or the close button (detail.source). It bubbles, crosses the shadow root and can be canceled to keep the dialog open.
dialogDocs.variantsText: actions sets how the footer buttons sit. inline puts them on the right, side by side, the primary last. stacked puts them one per line at full width, the primary on top, below the md breakpoint; at or above it, they stay inline.
dialogDocs.variantsCaption: The same dialog with actions inline and stacked, in a window narrower than the md breakpoint.
sizes: sm
Ceiling layout/dialog-sm (400). A choice or a short confirmation, without a destructive action.
md
Ceiling layout/dialog-md (560), the default. A short form.
lg
Ceiling layout/dialog-lg (720). A table, a long list or a two-column form.
dialogDocs.sizesCaption: The same wide content in each size: the dialog stops at the ceiling of its size.
relations: It always opens over the overlay/scrim veil; the veil is not part of the piece.
The footer combines the solid secondary nph-button, in color/secondary-on-dialog, with a primary or a danger. Color, state and focus of the buttons belong to nph-button.
The close button is the nph-button secondary, ghost, compact, with an icon only.
The lines are nph-separator in color/dialog-separator, softer than color/border.
The nph-alert-dialog builds on the nph-dialog without the close button.
Loading comes from the loading state of the nph-button in the footer.
dialogDocs.relationsCaption: The primary in loading while it publishes, next to the solid secondary.
anatomy: Background color/dialog, radius radius/overlay, shadow elevation/modal and padding space/overlay-padding. The height goes up to layout/dialog-max-height. The width hugs the content, from layout/dialog-min-width up to the ceiling of the size.
text/heading-md in color/dialog-foreground. It is the name of the dialog on screen.
text/body-md in color/muted-foreground, at space/stack-snug from the title. Optional.
nph-button secondary, ghost, compact, at the end of the line of the title. Optional.
nph-separator in color/dialog-separator, which separates long content from the header and the footer. Optional.
The area for fields, text or another composition. Its width sets the width of the dialog. It is the only part that scrolls.
Solid secondary nph-button and the primary or the danger, at space/inline-loose from each other, at space/stack plus space/stack-snug from what comes before. Optional.
accessibility: Semantics
A native dialog opened as modal (role=dialog, aria-modal), in the top layer; the rest of the page is inert while it is open.
Accessible name
The heading names the dialog (aria-labelledby) and the description completes it (aria-describedby). The close button carries close-label as its name.
Keyboard
Tab and Shift+Tab stay in the dialog. Esc asks to close it; a tooltip open inside it takes the first Esc.
Visible focus

On open, the focus goes to the first element with autofocus, otherwise to the first field of the content, then to the footer, then to the close button. On close, it goes back to the element that had it.
Contrast
Title, description and button text pass 4.5:1 on the background in both modes.
Touch target
The close button in compact meets the minimum of 24 by 24; the footer buttons stay in default.
Color is not the only signal
The title says the subject and the buttons say the actions; color only reinforces.

checkboxDocs.summary: A box with its own text, for the person to check independent options or turn one option on or off. It is a form control: a checked box submits its value with the form.
checkboxDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-checkbox spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P81. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: When the person can check more than one option, each independent.
For a single option, which the person turns on or off.
Indeterminate only on the item that summarizes a group checked in part: it is not an answer from the person.
The box alone only when the name is already in the context, such as a table cell, always with label.
whenNotToUse: When the options exclude each other: use nph-radio.
Around it, an nph-field only to give it a name: the box already brings its own text.
To mix checkbox and radio in the same group.
To put a link in the text, such as the terms of use: the link stays outside the piece.
To paint the box or the mark by hand: the piece takes its colors from tokens.
checkboxDocs.relationsText: Options that exclude each other are nph-radio; do not mix checkbox and radio in the same group. A group of boxes is composed with nph-field, which names the group and carries the error message; the box alone does not need nph-field to have a name. The mark is an nph-icon. The text is part of the piece, not an nph-label. nph-radio is planned and does not exist yet.
api: The current state, the Figma marcado true. It does not reflect: the checked attribute is the default state, the one a form reset goes back to. Once the person toggles the piece or code sets checked, the attribute no longer moves the current state.
A group checked only in part, the Figma marcado indeterminado. The box shows the minus mark whatever checked is. A click of the person clears it and toggles checked. It does not reflect.
The plain text next to the box, already localized: the name of the control. No link inside it. Without text, the piece is only the box.
The accessible name of the box alone; it becomes the aria-label of the inner checkbox. Required without text; with text, it is not used.
The error state: status/error border and aria-invalid. The error sentence stays outside the piece.
The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order and out of the form data. A disabled fieldset has the same effect. It wins over invalid.
The name of the entry in the form data: the attribute of the host.
What a checked piece submits: the attribute of the host, on when it is absent.
Read only: the form that owns the piece.

Native events, only when the person toggles the piece: input crosses the shadow root from the inner checkbox, and the host fires change, which bubbles. Setting checked or indeterminate from code fires nothing.
checkboxDocs.statesText: The Figma state property is the interaction: in code, only invalid and disabled are properties. Hover comes from the mouse and focus from the keyboard.
checkboxDocs.statesCaption: Text that wraps, with the box at the top; the box alone, checked; invalid, with the error sentence outside the piece.
states: Fill color/background; checked and indeterminate fill color/primary, with the check or minus mark in color/primary-foreground. Border color/input.
The whole piece responds, text included. Border color/input-hover; a checked or indeterminate box also takes state/hover-opacity.
Keyboard only. The box border turns focus/border and the focus/halo band covers the 24 × 24 touch area, with the radius focus/radius-inner.
Border status/error, checked or not. With focus, the border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error.
The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, text included, with the border color/input. Disabled wins over invalid.
The box sits at the top, centered on the first line; space/inline from the touch area to the text.
checkboxDocs.formText: nph-checkbox is a form control: the host joins the form of the page, as a native checkbox does.
formRules: Submits name=value; without the value attribute, the value is on.
Does not change what is submitted: checked decides.
Submits nothing, also inside a disabled fieldset.
Goes back to the checked attribute and clears indeterminate. No event fires.
There is no required and no constraint validation: invalid never blocks the submission. The error sentence belongs to the page or to nph-field.
anatomy: The check or minus icon of nph-icon, light, at icon/size-sm, in color/primary-foreground.
text/label-md in color/foreground: the name of the control and part of the piece, not an nph-label.
24 × 24: the box plus space/inline-tight on each side.
space/inline, from the edge of the touch area.
accessibility: Semantics
A native checkbox inside the piece: role checkbox, with the state unchecked, checked or mixed.
Accessible name
The text is the name. Without text, label becomes the aria-label. A label element outside, pointing to the piece, does not name the inner checkbox: the piece brings its own text.
Keyboard
One Tab stop; Space toggles and Enter does not. A disabled piece is skipped.
Visible focus
focus/border on the box and the focus/halo band on the touch area; on error, focus/halo-error.
Contrast
The box border, color/input, meets 3:1 against the background (WCAG 1.4.11); the mark meets 3:1 on color/primary.
Color is not the only signal
Checked and indeterminate show a mark; the error has its sentence outside the piece, and aria-invalid.
Touch target
24 × 24 around the 16 × 16 box.
Known limits

The checked fill, color/primary, is below 3:1 on the background in dark mode in the gerencial and rh brands; the box border meets it. focus/border is below 3:1 against the halo in light mode in the sistemas brand, as design.md records. With error and focus, status/error is below 3:1 against focus/halo-error in dark mode.

radioDocs.summary: The circle the person checks to choose one option in a group: checking one unchecks the others. The group is several nph-radio with the same name, inside an nph-field that names it.
radioDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-radio spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P82. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: When the options exclude each other: payment method, employment type, work shift.
When the group is small and fits the screen, with two to five options.
When every option must stay visible at the same time, so the person compares before choosing.
Always in a group of two or more, with one option checked when there is a reasonable default.
whenNotToUse: When the person can check more than one option: use nph-checkbox.
For a single option, alone: either options are missing, or the piece is nph-checkbox.
With more than five options: use nph-select.
When the person needs to uncheck by clicking again: offer a None option, or use nph-checkbox.
To mix radios and checkboxes in the same group.
radioDocs.relationsText: Above, nph-field names the group, such as Payment method, says it is required and carries the error message: the radio never shows a sentence of its own. Beside, the other radios of the same group, with the same name. Inside, nothing: the dot is a shape. nph-rich-option may use the radio with the text off, when the card is an exclusive choice.
api: The current state, the Figma marcado. It does not reflect. The checked attribute is the initial state and the one form.reset() returns to. Setting it from code unchecks the group and fires no event.
The group and the key in the form. Radios with the same name, in the same root and the same form, are one group. Reflects. Without a name, a radio is a group of one.
What the checked radio submits; on by default. Reflects.
The visible text, already localized; it is also the accessible name. Without it, the piece is only the 24 × 24 circle: the Figma mostrar rótulo off.
The accessible name when there is no text, never visible. Required then; aria-label or aria-labelledby on the host also count.
The error border, checked or not. Visual only: the error sentence and its announcement belong to nph-field.
The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order and the arrow keys. A disabled fieldset around it does the same. It wins over invalid.

The native events, fired on the host when the person checks the radio: input, which bubbles and crosses the shadow root, then change, which bubbles. Read event.target.value. A change from code never fires them.
radioDocs.statesText: The border says the state; the fill says the choice. Hover and focus are interaction: move the mouse over a radio, or reach it with Tab.
radioDocs.statesCaption: Unchecked and checked, at rest, with error and disabled.
states: Unchecked: color/background fill and color/input border. Checked: color/primary fill, the same border, and the color/primary-foreground dot.
The border is color/input-hover; checked, the circle also takes state/hover-opacity.
Keyboard only. The border is focus/border and a focus/halo halo covers the 24 × 24 touch area, fully round.
The border is status/error, checked or not; the checked fill stays color/primary.
The border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error.
state/disabled-opacity on the whole piece, text included. It does not combine with error: disabled wins.
radioDocs.groupText: The group is not an element: radios with the same name, in the same root and the same form, are one group. nph-field gives it the role, the name and the error; the radio owns the exclusivity, the arrow keys and its own Tab stop.
groupRules: Checks the radio, unchecks the others and fires input and change once. A click on the text checks it too.
A click on it changes nothing and fires no event; the click still bubbles. The person never unchecks by clicking again.
One stop per group: the checked radio or, with none checked, the first one that responds.
Down and right go to the next radio, up and left to the previous one, wrapping; the arrow moves the focus and checks. A disabled radio is skipped.
Setting checked unchecks the group and fires nothing. Two checked in the markup: the last one wins.
Without a name, or alone in its group, a radio still renders and warns in development: a radio never shows alone.
radioDocs.formText: The radio is form-associated, like nph-input: it takes part in the form around it without a native input of its own.
formRules: Only the checked radio enters the form, as name=value. With none checked, the group sends nothing.
Each radio returns to its checked attribute. Changing the attribute later moves the state only while nobody changed it.
The radios inside are disabled: out of Tab, with no click and at state/disabled-opacity.
There is no required on the radio: nph-field says the group is required.
anatomy: icon/size-sm (16), radius/full, border border/width in color/input, color/background fill.
8 × 8: the space left inside the circle after space/inline-tight, measured from its outer edge, in color/primary-foreground. No token of its own.
24 × 24: the circle plus space/inline-tight on each side.
text/label-md in color/foreground; it is the name of the control. It wraps, and the circle stays with the first line.
space/inline, from the edge of the touch area.
accessibility: Semantics
The host is role=radio, with aria-checked and aria-disabled, through ElementInternals. The group, role=radiogroup, comes from nph-field.
Accessible name
The text is the name of the control. Without text, label is the name. The group gets the name of nph-field.
Keyboard
One Tab stop per group; the arrow keys move and check; Space checks.
Visible focus
Border focus/border and the focus/halo halo on the touch area; with error, status/error and focus/halo-error.
Contrast
The circle outline in color/input: 3.23:1 in light and 6.58:1 in dark; the text, 21:1 and 14.73:1.
Color is not the only signal
The fill and the dot say the choice; the error has its sentence in nph-field.
Touch target
A 24 × 24 area around the 16 circle; the text also checks the option.
Known limits

Outside a radiogroup, the screen reader does not announce the group name or the position. invalid is not announced on the radio: aria-invalid belongs to the group. In light Sistemas, focus/border measures 2.92:1 against the halo.

dropdownMenuDocs.summary: A floating menu of secondary actions that opens attached to a button. The person chooses an action and the menu closes; a multiple choice and a switch keep it open.
dropdownMenuDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-dropdown-menu spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P92. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
dropdownMenuDocs.sourceStates: Figma item set 1365:57; design.md, color/primary-surface and dropdown/item-hover-icon-foreground.
whenToUse: For the secondary actions of a screen or of an item, such as rename, duplicate, move or sign out.
Single choice when only one option holds at a time, such as the view mode; multiple choice when several hold together, such as filters.
A tag to flag something new or a plan; a switch to turn something on or off without closing the menu; the profile header in the account menu.
Compact for a long, dense list; default in the other cases.
whenNotToUse: For the main navigation of the screen: the menu gathers secondary actions.
To hold a form value: use nph-select, nph-checkbox or nph-switch in the form.
For a switch in an action that navigates or closes the menu: use a common item.
For a destructive item on a common action: use the default type.
dropdownMenuDocs.relationsText: The menu opens from an nph-button, which stays outside the component and is named by for. The tag is an nph-badge, the avatar an nph-avatar, the separator an nph-separator, the box of a multiple choice an nph-checkbox and the switch an nph-switch; the color of each comes from the piece itself. The item is part of the menu: it is data of items, not a tag of its own.
api: The id of the element that opens the menu, in the same root as the menu: the nph-button outside the component. The menu writes aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on it.
The state, reflected. The menu opens and closes by itself; set it to show the menu open, with no focus move. It fires no event.
The entries, in order: items, group labels and separators. Property only.
The profile header: name, status and the photo of the avatar; null hides it. Property only.
default or compact, for the whole menu: the size of the item in Figma. Reflected.
The accessible name of the menu. Empty: the trigger names it.
The event the person fires by activating an item, with detail.value and detail.checked, null on a common item. It bubbles.
dropdownMenuDocs.entryText: Each entry of items is an item, a group label or a separator:
entry: Required. The label, on one line, cut with an ellipsis; the accessible name.
Text below the label, in text/caption.
The start icon, a core name of nph-icon; it turns solid on hover.
The photo of an nph-avatar at the start; an empty string draws the person icon.
The nph-switch at the end, without a label.
The state of a choice or a switch.
Plain text at the end, in text/caption.
The arrow at the end; the nested menu is out of scope.
The two states that take the focus and do not activate.
Names the group that follows it.
dropdownMenuDocs.variantsText: The item varies by severity and by selection. Destructive is only for the action that deletes or ends. Single choice shows the check at the end of the checked item; multiple choice shows the box at the start.
dropdownMenuDocs.variantsCaption: A common item, single choice, multiple choice and a destructive item.
dropdownMenuDocs.sizesText: default is the size for every menu; compact serves a long, dense list. The size is set on the whole menu.
dropdownMenuDocs.sizesCaption: size default, with rows of 36, and size compact, with rows of 28.
states: color/primary-surface (destructive: color/destructive-surface). The start icon and the submenu arrow turn solid in dropdown/item-hover-icon-foreground; the label keeps its color.
By keyboard: a border of border/width in color/primary and a halo in focus/halo, outside the row.
state/disabled-opacity on the whole row; it takes the focus and does not activate.
The nph-spinner takes the end of the row; the item is busy and does not activate.
dropdownMenuDocs.statesCaption: At rest, disabled and loading. Move the mouse over an item for hover.
dropdownMenuDocs.optionsText: Each option turns on in the entry: start icon or avatar, description, shortcut, counter, tag, switch and submenu arrow. The switch and the multiple choice keep the menu open.
dropdownMenuDocs.optionsCaption: Shortcut, description, counter, tag, switch, submenu arrow and avatar.
anatomy: Panel in color/popover with a border of border/width in color/dropdown-border, radius/container, elevation/dropdown, width layout/input-width and padding space/inline-tight.
Optional: avatar md, name in text/body-md and status in text/caption, with space/inline around and between; a separator below.
text/label-sm in color/muted-foreground, space/inline on the sides and space/inline-tight above and below.
Padding and gap space/inline, radius/inner, no background at rest; label in text/body-md and color/popover-foreground.
The nph-separator line between groups, with space/inline-tight above and below.
accessibility: Semantics
A menu with menuitem, menuitemradio and menuitemcheckbox items and named groups. The inner checkbox and switch are inert: the item carries the role and the state.
Accessible name
The item text. The description, the tag, the counter and the shortcut describe it. Support icons are not read.
Keyboard

On the trigger, Enter, Space and the down arrow open on the first item. In the menu, the arrows move, Home and End go to the ends, a letter finds an item, Enter and Space activate, Esc closes and Tab moves on.
Visible focus
The color/primary border carries the focus; the halo is decorative.
Color is not the only signal
The destructive item has the icon of the action; single choice shows the check; multiple choice the box; the switch the knob position; the tag carries text.
Touch target
The whole row of the item, above 24 by 24.
Known limits
On item hover, the box and the track do not take their own hover. aria-expanded on an nph-button does not reach its inner button. The nested menu is out of scope.

comboboxDocs.summary: The field where the person types to filter a list of options and picks one. It takes part in the form that contains it; the label, the help and the error message belong to nph-field.
comboboxDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-combobox spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P95. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
comboboxDocs.sourceDecisions: Task DSA-46, pending decisions D-1 to D-5; docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md › P95
comboboxDocs.description: Use nph-combobox when the list is long and searching by name is faster than scrolling. The chosen option shows as text in the field, with a button to clear it. It does not replace nph-select, for short lists without search, nor nph-multi-combobox, for several options. It accepts text outside the list only when the list offers the create row.
whenToUse: When the list is long and the person knows the name of what they look for: typing filters it.
Inside an nph-field, which gives the label, the help text and the error message.
With the status dot when each option has a state, written in the option text.
With creatable only when the list accepts new items; with the shortcuts footer on screens used a lot by keyboard.
default in most forms; large when the form uses tall fields.
whenNotToUse: For a short list that fits on the screen without search: use nph-select.
To pick several options: use nph-multi-combobox.
To offer create in a closed list: leave creatable off, and the list shows the nph-empty.
To change the color of the arrow area: for an error, use invalid through nph-field.
To use the status dot without a written state.
comboboxDocs.relationsText: The options are data, in options; the combobox draws each one as an nph-option, the option shared with nph-select. nph-field composes the label, the combobox, the help and the error message, and writes label, description, invalid and required on it. The empty list shows an nph-empty; the waiting list an nph-spinner; the groups take the group label and the separator of nph-dropdown-menu; the shortcuts footer takes nph-kbd keys.
api: The entries of the list, as data: options, group labels and separators. An invalid entry is left out.
default or large, reflected. The height of the field and the width of the arrow area change.

The current value: the value of the chosen option. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(). The value is kept until an option of that value arrives. Setting it from code fires nothing.
The typed text. Setting it from code writes it in the field and filters the list, and fires nothing.
The invitation before a choice, already localized, such as Search a country. It is not a name.
search, icon or avatar. search draws the magnifying glass; icon and avatar repeat the start of the chosen option, or the icon property and the empty avatar before a choice.
A core name of nph-icon, default globe: the start icon with start=icon.
The clear button and its accessible name. It erases the chosen option and the typed text.
contains, the list keeps the options whose text contains the typed text, with no difference of case or accent; none, the consumer filters options itself.
The waiting list: the nph-spinner and its accessible name.
The create row, which offers the typed text as a new item, and the words before the text.
The texts of the nph-empty when nothing matches.
Boolean, reflected. The list is open. Opening and closing fire no event.
As in a native field. With no chosen option, the entry is left out of the form data; required with no choice is valueMissing, with the message of the browser.
The erro state: the border becomes status/error and the field gets aria-invalid. The sentence belongs to nph-field.
Boolean, reflected. The whole piece fades, leaves the Tab order and the form data, and the list does not open.
The accessible name and description in text, never visible, written by nph-field.
Fired by the host, in this order, when the person changes the value: a choice, the clear button or the create row.
detail.query: the typed text changed. The consumer that filters searches with it.
detail.text: the person chose the create row. The value becomes the text; the consumer adds the option.
The shortcuts footer: nph-kbd keys and their words.
entries: The value for the form and the label, already localized. Both required in an option.
The helper text after the label.
The start of the nph-option: none, icon, avatar or dot, with its icon, photo or state.
The name of the group that follows it.
The line that closes a group.
comboboxDocs.invalidText: A size outside default and large, a start outside search, icon and avatar, an icon outside the core, or a filter outside contains and none: the combobox does not render and emits console.error in development. clearable without clear-label, creatable without create-label and loading without loading-label each emit one error.
comboboxDocs.sizesText: default in most forms; large when the form uses tall fields. The height of the field and the width of the arrow area change: control/height-default or control/height-large.
comboboxDocs.sizesCaption: default and large, with a chosen option.
states: Border color/input on color/background; the arrow area in color/accent, after a color/border divider.
Focus on the text: border focus/border and the focus/halo outside.
The focus look with the list open below the field and the arrow up.
Focus on the clear button: the ring follows only the button.
Border status/error, also on hover; with focus, the halo is focus/halo-error.
color/muted, border color/input and state/disabled-opacity on the whole piece; it wins over the error.
comboboxDocs.statesCaption: Placeholder, value with the clear button, error and disabled.
comboboxDocs.startText: search draws the magnifying glass, decorative. icon and avatar repeat the start of the chosen option: the avatar helps recognize the person.
comboboxDocs.listText: The list opens space/inline-tight below the field, with its width, and turns up when it does not fit below. It shows the options inside layout/max-list-height and scrolls above that. The focus stays on the text, which points to the active option.
listStates: The options that match, as nph-option.
The typed stretch in text/highlight-weight; the rest of the text in color/muted-foreground.
Options with the status dot and the written label.
Results under group labels, with the separator between groups.
The nph-spinner while the search answers.
The create row after the results, with the typed text.
The nph-empty when nothing matches in a closed list.
The optional footer with the keys, as nph-kbd.
comboboxDocs.statusCaption: status: the dot with the written state.
comboboxDocs.groupsCaption: grupos: group labels and the separator.
keyboard: Write in the field, open the list, filter it and make the first match active.
Closed: open on the chosen option, or on the first or the last. Open: move the active option, without wrapping.
Open: choose the active option and close. Closed, Enter submits the form.
Open: close without choosing. Closed: clear the typed text.
Close without choosing; the focus moves on.
Move the cursor in the text.
anatomy: The magnifying glass or an nph-icon icon/size-sm in color/muted-foreground, or an nph-avatar sm.
The placeholder, the typed text or the chosen option, in text/body-md; the placeholder in color/muted-foreground.
Button with the xmark nph-icon icon/size-sm and space/inline-tight around it.
border/width in color/border, right before the arrow area, space/inline after the content.
color/accent, control/height-* wide and the field height minus its borders; radius/none on the left and radius/control-inner on the right; chevron-down, or chevron-up open.
color/popover, border color/input, radius/container, padding space/inline-tight, maximum height layout/max-list-height, elevation/dropdown.
focus/border and focus/halo on the field, or around the clear button.
accessibility: Semantics
An editable combobox with list autocomplete: the text has role combobox and controls a listbox; each nph-option has role option and aria-selected.
Accessible name
The label of nph-field, or label; the placeholder is not a name. description is read with it: the help or the error sentence. The clear button has aria-label.
Keyboard and focus
The focus stays on the text and points to the active option with aria-activedescendant.
Contrast
Text 4.5:1 and the border 3:1, in light and dark mode; the arrow 3:1 on color/accent; the rest of the text outside the highlight in color/muted-foreground passes 4.5:1.
Color is not the only signal
The error comes as text in nph-field; the dot goes with the written state; the highlight changes the weight; the arrow turns up when the list opens.
Live region
The waiting and the empty lists sit in a status region: the person hears that the search found nothing.
Hidden parts
The magnifying glass, the divider, the arrow and the dot are hidden from the screen reader.

tableDocs.summary: The table to read and compare data in rows and columns, with caption, header, cells and footer. A row can open a detail or sub-levels. It does not sort, select, filter or paginate: that is the nph-data-table.
tableDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-table spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P97. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
whenToUse: To read and compare data in rows and columns, such as a statement, a report or a list of items.
framed for a table standing alone on the page; without the frame inside a card or panel, which already have a border.
A fixed header when the list is long inside a panel; horizontal scroll when the columns do not fit.
A two-level header to group columns of the same subject, such as accesses by channel.
An expanding row for the detail that does not fit in the row, such as an order and its items. It opens only through the chevron.
A tree, up to three levels, for a hierarchy, such as unit and sub-unit.
Size large on a touch screen or for a more relaxed reading; default otherwise.
whenNotToUse: To sort, select, filter or paginate: that is the nph-data-table.
To lay out the page: the table holds data.
With an empty cell when data is missing: use the no-value dash.
With numbers aligned to the start: align them to the end.
With an action written as a link: use the button in the cell.
tableDocs.relationsText: The composite cell receives other pieces, and each keeps its own rules: nph-avatar md, nph-badge light, nph-icon, the icon-only nph-button in the chevron, the actions and the more, the nph-button secondary light compact, nph-image, nph-skeleton and nph-tooltip. The more fires nph-row-action; opening the nph-dropdown-menu from it is a follow-up. With no row, the body holds the nph-empty. Sorting, selection, filtering and pagination belong to the nph-data-table.

tableDocs.rowsText: A row with detail opens the expanded item under it; a row with children opens the next level of the tree, up to three. Both open only through the chevron, which points right when closed and down when open; in the tree, the arrows and Enter on the row open and close it too. A two-level header groups columns of the same subject under a title.

accessibility: Semantics
A native table, with column headers, the group header over its columns and the footer. A table with a tree is a treegrid.
Accessible name
The caption title names the table and the description describes it; without a caption, label. The icon-only buttons and the chevron carry a name per row, such as Edit Ana Souza.
No value
The dash is read as no-value-label, such as sem valor.
Keyboard and focus

The scroll area takes the focus only when it overflows, so the keyboard can scroll it; the truncated text takes the focus and opens its tooltip. The ring is focus/border in table/focus-ring-width. In the tree, one row is the Tab stop: Tab goes on to the buttons and links of that row, the arrows move between rows and cells and open and close a row, Home and End go to the first and the last.
Open and level
In the tree, each row carries aria-level, its position among its siblings and, when it opens, aria-expanded. The chevron of an expanding row carries aria-expanded on the button host.
Color is not the only signal
The status has a shape and a name, the badge always has text, the link is underlined, and Delete is written in the menu.
Contrast
Text and link pass AA over background, stripe, header and hover. Exception: the rating star is below 3:1 in light; the score stays as a number.
Touch target
The chevron and the more of the mixed actions are 28 by 28; Edit and more of the actions are 36 by 36. On a touch screen, use size large.
