claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--sizes: The three sizes, with a photo and without: a square of 24, 32 and 40 px with a rounded corner, never a circle.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--photo: A valid src fills the frame and replaces the person icon; the border stays over the picture.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--no-pho: Without src, or with an empty one, the person icon shows at the icon size of each avatar size.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--photo-: A src that does not load keeps the person icon, with no event and no error.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--border: The avatar draws its own border over the photo: overlapped by hand, with a negative margin on a plain wrapper, the neighbors stay separated. The group itself is nph-avatar-stack, which uses the same border.
claims.components-nph-avatar-validation--access: With label the avatar is an image named by it; without label it is hidden from the screen reader and the name beside it speaks.
claims.components-nph-avatar-stack-validation--: The three sizes, without and with the count: the group writes its size on every avatar, overlaps them by avatar/overlap and draws the count in the same size.
Two to five avatars, with and without the count: what the Figma mostrar 3º, mostrar 4º, mostrar 5º and mostrar contagem turn on.
Photos and no photo in the same group: each avatar keeps its own type, and its border keeps the neighbors apart. The group draws no ring.
The count starts as a square of the avatar size and grows with the number, keeping its height and its text role.
The group is one image named by label, with the names and the total; the avatars and the count are not read.
claims.components-nph-badge-validation--matrix: Each severity value in both emphasis values, without an icon.
claims.components-nph-badge-validation--with-ic: The icon comes before the text, at icon/size-sm, in the text color.
claims.components-nph-badge-validation--two-wor: One or two words stay on a single line: the badge does not wrap.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--matrix: Each severity and emphasis pair that exists, at the default size. Move the mouse over a button to see hover.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--sizes: The three sizes, with text and with an icon only. The text is label-md in all of them.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--icons: Start icon, end icon and both together, at icon/size-sm, and an icon-only button. Move the mouse over a button: the icons turn solid.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--disabl: Disabled: the whole button at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--loadin: Loading: the spinner takes the place of the start icon, and the text stays.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--shapes: Square and circular corners of the icon-only button, in each size and emphasis: the size stays. Use Tab to see the focus follow the round corners.
claims.components-nph-button-validation--toolti: Every icon-only button shows its label in a tooltip: Tab opens it at once, the pointer after motion/hover-delay. A disabled button gets none; a loading one keeps it.
claims.components-nph-input-otp-validation--mat: Six and four cells, in the default and large sizes: every cell is a square of the control height, space/inline apart.
claims.components-nph-input-otp-validation--sta: Default, invalid and disabled on every cell, and disabled winning over invalid; the error sentence belongs to nph-field.
claims.components-nph-input-otp-validation--cha: A numeric code, a code with letters and numbers, a partial code with empty cells, and masked, with a dot in place of each character.
claims.components-nph-input-otp-validation--int: Type or paste a code: the active cell follows the caret, a pasted code replaces the value, and input and change are shown below the field.
claims.components-nph-input-otp-validation--exa: The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: a code sent by e-mail and a wrong code, in the nph-field, and the touch screen, with size large.
claims.components-nph-kbd-validation--single-ke: One key per piece, through the text property.
claims.components-nph-kbd-validation--combinati: A combination joins one piece per key, side by side.
claims.components-nph-kbd-validation--mac-combi: The same combination on macOS, with the system symbols. The application picks the set by the person's system; the piece does not detect it.
claims.components-nph-separator-validation--hor: Between stacked items, the line fills the width.
claims.components-nph-separator-validation--ver: Between side-by-side items, the line fills the height.
claims.components-nph-spinner-validation--sizes: sm inside a button or field; md in a content area.
claims.components-nph-spinner-validation--acces: With text beside it, the spinner is decorative; without text, it has an accessible name.
claims.components-nph-spinner-validation--inval: size="lg" does not exist: nothing is drawn, and the area below stays empty on purpose.
claims.components-nph-toggle-group-validation--: Two and three buttons, with text and icon only, in a group named by its subject; each button keeps its own state.
Single selection: it starts empty or with a value, checking one unchecks the others, and a click on the checked button does nothing.
Multiple selection: each button checks and unchecks on its own, and the value gathers the checked ones.
Disabled and invalid stay on each button: the group adds nothing, and the error message stays outside it.
A click changes the selection and fires nph-value-change with detail.value, shown below the group; setting value from code does not fire it.
The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Alignment, Formatting and View.
claims.components-nph-togglebutton-validation--: Pressed off and on, valid and invalid, with text. Move the mouse over a button to see hover and press Tab to see focus.
Start and end icons: auto swaps xmark and check with the state, none draws no icon and a core name is one fixed icon.
Icon only: one icon, a label as the accessible name, 50 by 36 px and not square, side by side with one on.
Disabled: the whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order; disabled wins over invalid.
Invalid: the track border is status/error, pressed or not, with text or icon only; the message stays outside the piece.
A click toggles the piece and fires nph-change with detail.pressed, shown below the button; setting pressed from code does not fire it.
The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Option off, Option on and Icon set.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--one-l: The open balloon above an element, with a one-line text, as in the Figma example.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--two-l: The open balloon with a two-line text: in every language it takes exactly two lines.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--sides: The four sides, top by default, with the action name of an icon-only button, in light and in dark mode.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--flip: The balloon flips to the opposite side when it does not fit on the preferred one.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--focus: Keyboard focus opens the balloon and Esc closes it, with the focus staying on the element.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--hover: Hover after a short wait and keyboard focus at once open the balloon on any element that receives focus: a button, a link and a field.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--acces: On an icon-only button the balloon text is the accessible name of the action, announced once.
claims.components-nph-tooltip-validation--focus: The balloon goes only on an element that receives focus: a disabled button gets none.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--matrix: size × state of the set: placeholder, value, error, disabled and disabled with error. Move the mouse over a field for hover and click it for focus.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--types: The five types of D1, each with a value it accepts. Password, number and mask are out of v1.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--icons: Start and end icons, light, at icon/size-sm: none, start, end and both. The end icon only swaps the art; the action is always to clear.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--clear: The clear button shows with a value. A click, Enter or Space empties it, brings the focus back to the field and fires input and change.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--form-as: The host is labelable and takes part in the form: the label focuses it, submit sends name=value, reset restores the value attribute, and a disabled fieldset leaves it out.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--error-a: The precedence of D5: error keeps its border on hover and focus; disabled wins over error.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--width: The default width is layout/input-width; the field stretches to its parent, with no minimum (D6).
claims.components-nph-input-validation--invalid: Invalid input draws nothing: a type out of v1, a size that does not exist, an icon outside the core. icon-end without clear-label draws the field without the button.
claims.components-nph-input-validation--example: The three required examples of the accepted frame: Search, Field with a label and Error, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--matr: The states of the set: placeholder and value, error, readonly, disabled, and the precedence of disabled over readonly and of readonly over error. Move the mouse for hover, click for focus.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--foot: The footer shows with a counter or an action, the counter at the start and the actions at the end; disabled reaches the actions; readonly draws no footer.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--heig: Empty, the field has layout/textarea-min-height; it grows with the text and stops at layout/textarea-max-height, where the text scrolls inside.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--form: The host takes part in the form: submit sends name=value with its line breaks, Enter writes a line and does not send, reset restores the value attribute and a disabled fieldset leaves it out.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--in-f: Inside nph-field, the field gives the label, the help, the error and the support-line counter, and the footer stays off.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--widt: The width is layout/input-width by default; it stretches to the parent, with no minimum.
claims.components-nph-textarea-validation--exam: The three required examples of the frame, each in light and dark mode: Comment, Description in a form and Long text.
claims.components-nph-empty-validation--with-de: The heading says what is missing and the description says what to do, as in the board; the illustration follows the color scheme.
claims.components-nph-empty-validation--heading: With an empty description only the heading remains, for when there is nothing to suggest.
claims.components-nph-empty-validation--surface: The heading and the description pass 4.5:1 on color/background and on color/popover, in light and in dark mode.
claims.components-nph-empty-validation--combobo: The search with no result in the nph-combobox list, in a frame until the nph-combobox exists.
claims.components-nph-empty-validation--invalid: Without a heading the piece draws nothing and has no visual fallback.
claims.components-nph-image-validation--sizes: The seven sizes, with an image and without: squares of 24, 32, 48, 64, 96 and 128 px with a rounded corner, and media on the content width of 256 px.
claims.components-nph-image-validation--ratios: media takes 1:1, 4:3 and 16:9 on the same width, 256 by 256, 192 or 144 px; a square size ignores the ratio and stays square.
claims.components-nph-image-validation--states: The state derives from src: empty without it, the spinner and no border while the image loads, the image filling the frame once loaded, and the frame again when it fails. Empty and error draw the frame only until their illustrations arrive.
claims.components-nph-image-validation--interac: A clickable image is a button: move the mouse over it for the veil and the eye, press Tab for the focus ring. Disabled fades the whole piece and takes the button out of the Tab order.
claims.components-nph-image-validation--accessi: With alt the image is announced by its description; with an empty alt it is hidden from the screen reader and the text beside it speaks. A clickable image gives the alt to its button.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--matrix: Error, required mark and information icon, the three variant axes of the set, in light and in dark mode.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--message: The message line: not drawn when empty; the help in text/caption; the error replaces it, with no icon; a long text wraps.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--counter: The counter at the end of the help line, alone, and on a line of its own below the error.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--width: The field takes layout/field-width by default and stretches with its container; the control fills it.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--group: A group of checkboxes and a group of radios, stacked, named and described by the field.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--disable: Disabled: the control fades, the label and the message line do not; disabled wins over error.
claims.components-nph-field-validation--control: What the field writes on its control (P83): the name, the description, invalid, required and disabled.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--matrix: Off and on, valid, invalid and disabled, with a label. Move the mouse over a piece to see hover and press Tab to see focus on the track.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--label: The label after the track; without text, only the track, named by label; a long label wraps to the available width, with the track at the top, aligned with the first line.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--disabl: Disabled: the whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order, on or off; disabled wins over invalid.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--invali: Invalid: the track outline is status/error, on or off, with a label or only the track; the error sentence stays outside the piece.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--intera: A click toggles the piece and fires the native input and change; checked is read from the target and shown below the piece. Setting checked from code fires nothing.
claims.components-nph-switch-validation--exampl: The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Single setting, Preferences and Unavailable setting.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--matrix: orientation × mode × state of the set: default, error and disabled. Move the mouse over a thumb for the balloon and press Tab for focus.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--option: The optional parts, each on its own and together: text, limits, marks, inputs and steppers. In the vertical orientation only text and limits exist.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--keyboa: The arrows move one step, Page Up and Page Down a tenth, Home and End go to the ends; a drag moves the nearest thumb. input fires while the value moves and change when it settles.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--form-a: The host takes part in the form: single submits name=value, range two entries under the same name, reset restores the value attributes, and a disabled fieldset leaves it out.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--inside: Inside nph-field, the field gives the label, the help and the error; the slider shows the error state and reads the sentence as its description.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--invali: Invalid input draws nothing: an orientation or a mode that does not exist, min not below max, a step of zero. marks in the vertical orientation is not drawn; the rest renders.
claims.components-nph-slider-validation--exampl: The three required examples of the accepted board: Brightness, Price range and Volume, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-select-validation--matrix: size × state: placeholder, value, error, disabled and both, with the arrow area in color/accent. Move the mouse for hover, press Tab for focus.
claims.components-nph-select-validation--start: The start of the trigger (D4): none, icon and avatar, before a choice and with the start of the chosen option; the dot of an option never goes to the trigger.
claims.components-nph-select-validation--option: The option: the four starts, the secondary text, active with the hover look, selected with the check winning over active, disabled, and the dot in every state (D5, D6).
claims.components-nph-select-validation--open: The open list: space/inline-tight below the trigger, with its width, the arrow up and the chosen option with the check (D1, D2).
claims.components-nph-select-validation--list-h: The height of the list (D9): 8 whole options inside layout/max-list-height; with avatars, 7 whole options and 8 px of the 8th; scroll above that.
claims.components-nph-select-validation--text-o: Trigger value, option label and secondary text stay on one line with an ellipsis (D3).
claims.components-nph-select-validation--form-a: The host takes part in the form: submit sends name=value, reset restores the value attribute, a choice fires input and change, and a disabled fieldset disables it.
claims.components-nph-select-validation--invali: Invalid input draws nothing: a size that does not exist, a start that does not exist and an icon outside the core.
claims.components-nph-select-validation--exampl: The three required examples of the frame, in nph-field: Department, Owner (open) and Required with no choice, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-dialog-validation--short-: Short form in md, the default size: title, description, content area and actions, in light and in dark mode.
Short confirmation in sm, with no content area: the header text sets the width, up to the ceiling.
claims.components-nph-dialog-validation--wide-c: Wide content in lg, a list, with both lines on: only the content scrolls.
claims.components-nph-dialog-validation--stacke: Stacked actions below the md breakpoint: one button per line, the primary on top.
claims.components-nph-dialog-validation--loadin: The primary in loading while the action finishes, next to the solid secondary of the dialog.
claims.components-nph-dialog-validation--focus-: Opening moves the focus into the dialog; Esc or the close button close it and the focus goes back to the button that opened it.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--matr: Unchecked, checked and indeterminate against default, invalid and disabled, with text and as the box alone.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--text: Text that wraps: the box sits at the top, centered on the first line, with space/inline to the text.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--box-: The box alone, 24 × 24, named by label, for a context that already gives the name.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--inva: The error border on the box; the error sentence stays outside the piece.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--disa: The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, also inside a disabled fieldset; disabled wins over invalid.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--form: A checked box submits name=value with the form; reset goes back to the checked attribute.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--inte: A click or Space toggles the box and fires input and change; a click on indeterminate checks it.
claims.components-nph-checkbox-validation--exam: The three required examples of the frame: consent, preferences and group selection.
claims.components-nph-radio-validation--matrix: Unchecked and checked, in the default, error and disabled states, and with the text off: the circle, the fill, the border and the dot of each one.
claims.components-nph-radio-validation--two-lin: The text wraps to the available width; the circle stays at the top, centered on the first line, and does not center on the block of text.
claims.components-nph-radio-validation--interac: One Tab stop for the group; the arrow keys move and check, skipping the disabled radio; the person checking a radio fires change, shown below the group.
claims.components-nph-radio-validation--form: The form receives only the checked radio, under its name; reset returns to the radio checked at the start.
claims.components-nph-radio-validation--example: The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: Payment method, Employment type and Work shift.
claims.components-nph-dropdown-menu-validation-: A common item, single choice with the check, multiple choice with the box and a destructive item, open in light and dark. Move the mouse over an item to see hover and the solid icon; use the arrows to see focus.
Every item option: start icon, description, shortcut, counter, tag, switch, submenu arrow and avatar, in a row that keeps its height.
A disabled item at state/disabled-opacity and a loading item with the spinner at the end; neither activates. Hover and focus come from the mouse and the keyboard.
size default, with rows of 36, and size compact, with rows of 28, for the whole menu.
The profile header above the items, with a separator below it, a group label and the destructive Sign out.
The trigger opens the menu; activating an item fires nph-item-select, whose value and checked show below the trigger. A switch keeps the menu open.
The three required examples, each in light and dark mode: the account menu, single choice with a counter, and tag, switch and destructive.
claims.components-nph-combobox-validation--matr: size × state: placeholder, value, value with the clear button, error, disabled and both, with the divider and the arrow area in color/accent. Move the mouse for hover, press Tab for focus and again for the clear button.
claims.components-nph-combobox-validation--star: The start of the field: the magnifying glass, an icon and an avatar, before a choice and with the start of the chosen option.
claims.components-nph-combobox-validation--list: The seven states of the list, open: results, search with the typed stretch highlighted, status, groups, loading, create and empty; and the shortcuts footer (D-1 to D-3).
claims.components-nph-combobox-validation--form: The host takes part in the form: submit sends name=value, reset restores the value attribute, a choice fires input and change, and a disabled fieldset disables it.
claims.components-nph-combobox-validation--inva: Invalid input draws nothing: a size, a start and a filter that do not exist, and an icon outside the core.
claims.components-nph-combobox-validation--exam: The three required examples of the board, in nph-field: chosen option at rest, search with the typed stretch highlighted and search waiting for the answer, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--sizes: The two sizes: default with the 40 px row and the cell sides at 12 px; large with the 44 px row and the sides at 16 px.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--frame: Without the frame and with it: the border, the corner and the last row that leaves its divider to the frame.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--sticky-: The fixed header: the body scrolls up to its maximum height and the header stays, with the line under it.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--row-sta: The stripe on every other row, the grid between the columns, and the hover on the whole row under the pointer.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--caption: The caption with description, total and action names the table; without a caption, the label names it; a table that does not fit becomes a focusable scroll area.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--cell-co: Every composite cell with the piece it takes: person, badge, icon and text, status, rating, link, thumbnail, truncated text, button, actions, mixed actions, loading and the no-value dash.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--expandi: The expanding row: closed, open with the expanded item, and loading, each opened only through its chevron.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--tree: The tree in three levels: each level indents, and a row without children keeps the space of the chevron so the text aligns. It is a treegrid: the arrows move between rows and cells, and open and close a level.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--two-lev: The two-level header: the group title above the columns it groups, with the same header piece.
claims.components-nph-table-validation--empty-b: With no row, the body holds the nph-empty and the header stays visible.
claims.components-nph-multi-combobox-validation: size × state: placeholder, chips on one line, chips on several lines, the counter, error, disabled and both. Move the mouse for hover, press Tab for each remove button and for the text.
The chip: the pill in color/primary-surface, the start icon of each kind and tag for an option with none (D-3), the disabled chip, and a long label on one line with an ellipsis (D3).
The nph-combobox list with each option in the checkbox marker, checked when chosen and without the selected background: results, search with the typed stretch highlighted, groups and empty (D-1).
The host takes part in the form: submit sends one entry per chosen option, reset restores the default values, a change fires input and change, and a disabled fieldset disables it.
A size that does not exist draws nothing; chips without remove-label have no remove button, and a counter without subject is drawn alone, each with one error.
The three required examples of the board, in nph-field: two options chosen at rest, in focus with typed text and the list open, and many options on several lines, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-sidebar-item-validation--: type × state of the item: link, counter, group closed and open, at rest, active and disabled. Active does not exist in a group. Move the mouse for hover and press Tab for the focus.
The subitem with options no and yes, at rest, active and disabled: label only, and the arrow to the right with options (D-4).
The rail button with the counter off and on, at rest, active and disabled: the counter on the top end corner (D-1), with an outline when active (D-2).
The balloon with the full name of a cut label, on hover and focus; more actions at the end of the line, on hover and focus, opening its menu; the balloon of the rail button, always on.
Invalid input draws nothing: an active group, a counter with text, a subitem without href and a rail button without label, each with one error.
The three required examples of the board: main menu with current page and counter, group open with subitems, and collapsed menu with rail buttons, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-pagination-validation--ma: type × position: the six types at the start, in the middle and at the end of a list of ten pages. The arrow without a destination is disabled, in place; the current page has background and bold. Move the mouse for hover and the balloon, and press Tab for the focus.
claims.components-nph-pagination-validation--go: Go to page beside the bar with first and last: type a page and press Enter. Past the end it goes to the last page.
claims.components-nph-pagination-validation--in: Invalid input draws nothing: a type that does not exist, no page count, go to page outside edges and an arrow without its label, each with one error.
claims.components-nph-pagination-validation--ex: The three required examples of the board: data table footer in the middle of the list, search result on the first page and card header on the last page, each in light and dark mode.
claims.components-nph-chip-validation--removabl: The removable chip by content, size and state: text, icon and avatar, in compact and default, at rest, marked, read only, invalid and disabled. Hover, focus and active are interaction states: move the mouse over the X and press Tab to see them; the component tests measure them.
claims.components-nph-chip-validation--severiti: The status colors, which exist on a removable chip with text only: success, warning, error, info and help, in both sizes, at rest and disabled. The label carries the status in words, and the X stays in the foreground color.
claims.components-nph-chip-validation--selectab: The selectable chip by content, size and state: text, icon and counter, in compact and default, at rest, disabled, selected and selected disabled. The selected chip shows the X. Hover, focus and active are interaction states: move the mouse over the chip and press Tab to see them.
claims.components-nph-chip-validation--long-tex: A label wider than the chip is cut with an ellipsis, in both types and both sizes. The whole text shows in a balloon on hover and on keyboard focus: move the mouse over the chip and press Tab to see it.
claims.components-nph-chip-validation--invalid-: Invalid input draws nothing: a type or a severity that does not exist, an icon outside the core, two contents at once, a counter on a removable chip, an avatar on a selectable chip, a state in a status severity and an X with no remove-label, each with one error.
claims.components-nph-chip-validation--examples: The three mandatory examples of the documentation: applied filters in the line of the toolbar, values chosen in a field with one invalid, and quick filters that the person checks and unchecks, each in light and dark mode.

multiComboboxDocs.summary: The field where the person searches a closed list and picks several options, shown as chips inside the field. It takes part in the form that contains it; the label, the help and the error message belong to nph-field.
multiComboboxDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-multi-combobox spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P96. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
multiComboboxDocs.sourceDecisions: Task DSA-31, decisions D1 to D3 and pending decisions D-1 to D-4; docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md › P96
multiComboboxDocs.description: Use nph-multi-combobox when the person picks more than one option from a known list and needs to see what is already chosen without opening the list. Each choice becomes a chip with a button to remove it. It does not replace nph-select or nph-combobox, which keep a single option, and it does not accept text outside the list.
whenToUse: When the person picks several options from a closed list, such as people, teams or tags.
When seeing what is already chosen, in the field itself, helps to check and to remove.
Inside an nph-field, which gives the label, the help text and the error message.
With counter when the field needs to stay on one line, as in a filter, a table or a toolbar; the open list shows every choice.
With chip-icon when the options are of different kinds, such as tag and team.
default in most forms; large when the form uses tall fields.
whenNotToUse: To pick a single option: use nph-select or nph-combobox.
For free text or options that are not in the list: use nph-input.
With counter when the person needs to check each choice: let the chips go to several lines.
To put an avatar in the chip: mark the kind of the option with chip-icon.
With a fixed width in pixels: use layout/multi-combobox-width or the width of the form.
multiComboboxDocs.relationsText: The list is the nph-combobox list: the same entries, search, groups and highlight. Each option is an nph-option with the checkbox marker, an inert nph-checkbox checked when the option is chosen. The counter is an nph-badge. nph-field composes the label, the field, the help and the error message, and writes label, description, invalid and required on it.
api: The entries of the list, as data, as in nph-combobox: options, group labels and separators. An invalid entry is left out.
default or large, reflected. Only the minimum height changes.
The chosen values, a list, in the order the person chose them. A value with no option is kept until its option arrives. Setting it from code fires nothing.
The values of form.reset(). While the choice is not changed, setting it moves value too.
The typed text. Setting it from code writes it in the field and filters the list, and fires nothing.
The invitation while nothing is chosen, already localized, such as Search countries. It is not a name.
The counter mode: the field stays on one line with the subject, such as Countries, and an nph-badge with how many are chosen.
Each chip shows the icon of its option, or tag for an option with no icon.
The word the remove button says before the option, such as Remove: the button reads Remove Brazil.
The texts of the nph-empty when nothing matches.
Boolean, reflected. The list is open. Opening and closing fire no event.
One entry name=value per chosen option, as a select multiple; required with nothing chosen is valueMissing, with the message of the browser.
The erro state: the border becomes status/error and the field gets aria-invalid. The sentence belongs to nph-field.
Boolean, reflected. The whole piece fades, leaves the Tab order and the form data, the chips lose the remove button, and the list does not open.
The accessible name and description in text, never visible, written by nph-field.
Fired by the host, in this order, when the person changes the choice: an option checked or unchecked, or a chip removed.
entries: The value for the form and the label, already localized. Both required in an option.
The helper text after the label.
The start of the nph-option: none, icon, avatar or dot. The icon also goes to the chip with chip-icon.
The name of the group that follows it.
The line that closes a group.
multiComboboxDocs.invalidText: A size outside default and large: the field does not render and emits console.error in development. Chips without remove-label have no remove button, and counter without subject draws the counter alone, each with one error.
multiComboboxDocs.sizesText: default in most forms; large when the form uses tall fields. Only the minimum height changes: control/height-default or control/height-large. The field grows when the chips go to another line.
multiComboboxDocs.sizesCaption: default and large, with two options chosen.
states: Border color/input on color/background; the magnifying glass and the arrow in color/muted-foreground.
Focus on the text, and the list open: border focus/border and the focus/halo outside.
Focus on a remove button: the ring follows only the 24 × 24 target.
Border status/error, also on hover; with focus, the halo is focus/halo-error.
color/muted, border color/input and state/disabled-opacity on the whole piece; the chips in color/muted with no remove button. It wins over the error.
multiComboboxDocs.chipText: Each chosen option is a chip: a pill in color/primary-surface, radius/full, with the label in text/label-sm and color/primary-on-surface and the remove button at the end. A long label stays on one line with an ellipsis, and the chip stops before the end of the field (D3). The chip is internal: it is not a piece of its own.
chipStates: color/primary-surface, the label in color/primary-on-surface, the remove button.
The focus ring around the remove button only.
color/muted, the label and the icon in color/muted-foreground, no remove button.
multiComboboxDocs.chipCaption: Without and with chip-icon: the icon of each kind, and tag for an option with no icon.
multiComboboxDocs.counterText: With counter, the field stays on one line: after the magnifying glass, the subject in text/body-md, such as Countries, and an nph-badge primary solid with how many options are chosen. The subject does not change with each choice (D1). The open list shows every choice.
multiComboboxDocs.listText: The list is the nph-combobox list. It opens space/inline-tight below the field, with its width, and turns up when it does not fit below. Each option shows a checkbox, checked when the option is chosen, without the selected background. The list stays open while the person checks and unchecks; the focus stays on the text, which points to the active option.
listStates: The options that match, each with its checkbox.
Results under group labels, with the separator between groups.
multiComboboxDocs.searchCaption: The typed stretch highlighted, two options checked.
keyboard: Write in the field, open the list, filter it and make the first match active.
Closed: open on the first or the last option. Open: move the active option, without wrapping.
Open: check or uncheck the active option and keep the list open. Closed: submit the form.
Close the list; with the list closed, clear the typed text.
Close the list without choosing and move on. Before the text, Tab reaches each remove button; Enter or Space removes the option.
anatomy: color/background, border border/width in color/input, radius/control, width layout/multi-combobox-width, minimum height control/height-default or control/height-large, padding space/control-padding on the sides and space/inline-tight above and below, gap space/inline.
One chosen option per chip, space/inline-tight between them in both directions; they go down to the next line when space runs out.
nph-icon xmark, icon/size-sm, in the chip text color, with space/inline-tight around it: a 24 × 24 target.
text/body-md in color/foreground after the chips; the placeholder in color/muted-foreground only with nothing chosen.
nph-icon chevron-down, icon/size-sm, color/muted-foreground. It says there is a list to open.
The nph-combobox list, with the options in the checkbox marker.
Only when the text or a remove button has the focus.
accessibility: Semantics
The text field has role combobox and controls a listbox with aria-multiselectable; each option has aria-selected. The host is form-associated.
Accessible name
From nph-field, or from an associated label. Each remove button is named by remove-label and the option it removes.
Focus
The focus stays on the text; the active option is pointed to by aria-activedescendant. A click on the label goes to the text, not to a remove button.
Hidden parts
The magnifying glass, the arrow, the chip icon, the remove icon and the box of the option are hidden from the screen reader.
Touch target
The whole field opens the list; each remove button has its own 24 × 24 area.
Color is not the only signal
The error comes with the nph-field message; a chosen option is checked; the disabled field also loses the remove buttons.

sidebarItemDocs.summary: The line of the lateral menu that leads the person to a page or opens a group of pages. It comes as the first-level item, the second-level subitem and the rail button, which plays the role of the item when the menu is collapsed.
sidebarItemDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-sidebar-item, nph-sidebar-subitem and nph-sidebar-rail-button spec sheets, design.md for the tokens and docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md for P98. The DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0 Figma file is the visual source. No rule is created here.
sidebarItemDocs.sourceFrame: Figma, board nph-sidebar-item (1366:2), documentation 2723:460, sets 2251:51271, 2251:51312 and 2251:51328
sidebarItemDocs.sourceRail: nph-sidebar-rail-button spec sheet; task DSA-53, pending decisions D-1 and D-2; docs/decisoes-tecnicas.md › P98
sidebarItemDocs.sourceAccessibility: Figma, documentation 2723:460; nph-sidebar-item.test.ts, nph-sidebar-subitem.test.ts and nph-sidebar-rail-button.test.ts
sidebarItemDocs.description: Use nph-sidebar-item inside nph-sidebar to move between the areas of the product. The item is the first-level line; the subitem is the second-level line, inside a group; the rail button shows only the icon when the menu is collapsed. It does not replace nph-panel-menu, which organizes the navigation inside the content, nor nph-dropdown-menu, which opens actions and choices.
whenToUse: With type link, to lead to a product page.
With counter, when the page has something to look at, such as new messages or tasks.
With type group, to gather pages of the same subject under an item that opens and closes.
With tooltip, when the label can be cut, to show the full name.
With more actions, as a shortcut of the item actions for mouse and keyboard, always with the same actions on the destination page.
Disabled, when the page exists but the person has no access now.
whenNotToUse: As an action button, such as save or delete: use nph-button.
As a group for one page only: use type link.
To choose an option or open actions in a menu: use nph-dropdown-menu.
To organize the navigation inside the content: use nph-panel-menu.
With text in the counter: the counter shows a number only; for a short label, use nph-badge.
With more actions as the only path to an action: on touch it does not appear.
api: link (default) leads to a page; group opens and closes the subitems below it. The Figma counter type is a link with counter; group-closed and group-open are group with expanded.
The text of the line, already localized: one line, with an ellipsis when it does not fit. It is the accessible name.
A core name of nph-icon, at icon/size-md: light at rest, solid when active or in an open group.
The page the link leads to. Required in a link that is not disabled; a group has none.
The current page: aria-current="page", its color, the solid icon and text/label-md. Only one item is active, and never a group.
The group is open: aria-expanded, the arrow up, its color, the solid icon and text/label-md. Only in a group.
A whole number from zero up, read as text inside the name of the link. Only in a link.
The page exists, but the person has no access now: state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order, no balloon and no more actions.
The text of the nph-tooltip with the full name, on hover and focus. It does not follow label; empty turns it off.
The entries of the nph-dropdown-menu of more actions, and the accessible name of its button. With actions and no actions-label, the item does not render.
Fired when the person opens or closes a group, with detail.expanded. It bubbles and crosses shadow roots. Setting expanded from code fires nothing.
The action the person chose in the menu of more actions, fired again on the host with the detail of nph-dropdown-menu. It bubbles.
sidebarItemDocs.invalidText: A type outside link and group, an icon outside the core, a link without href, a group with href, counter or active, a counter that is not a whole number and actions without actions-label: the item does not render and emits console.error in development, once per cause.
sidebarItemDocs.typesCaption: link, counter, group closed and group open.
types: A link to a page with something to look at, such as new messages or tasks.
Gathers pages of the same subject; the arrow down says it opens.
The subitems show right below it; the arrow up says it closes.
sidebarItemDocs.statesCaption: At rest, active and disabled. Move the mouse for hover and press Tab for the focus.
states: No background: the line shows the panel. Label and icon in sidebar/item-foreground, the label in text/body-md.
No background: the label and the icon in sidebar/item-foreground-active, the solid icon and text/label-md. It does not exist in a group.
Border border/width in color/primary and halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo around the whole line, keyboard only.
The whole line at state/disabled-opacity, no hover, out of the Tab order.
sidebarItemDocs.subitemText: nph-sidebar-subitem is the second-level line, inside an open group: the label only, at control/height-default, with space/inline top and bottom and sidebar/item-padding on the sides. With options, the arrow to the right says it leads to a list of options; the subitem stays a link (D-4).
sidebarItemDocs.subitemCaption: Active, at rest, and with options.
subitemApi: The text of the line, already localized, one line with an ellipsis. It is the accessible name.
The page the subitem leads to. Required unless disabled.
The current page: aria-current="page", sidebar/item-foreground-active and text/label-md.
The arrow chevron-right at icon/size-sm, visual only.
state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order, no balloon.
The text of the nph-tooltip with the full name, on hover and focus.
sidebarItemDocs.railText: nph-sidebar-rail-button plays the role of the item when nph-sidebar is collapsed: a square of sidebar/rail-button-size with the icon only. The label is its name and the text of the balloon, which is always on. The counter sits on the top end corner (D-1) and, when active, gains an outline in sidebar/panel-background (D-2).
sidebarItemDocs.railCaption: At rest, active, with the counter, active with the counter, and disabled.
railApi: The name of the page, required: the aria-label of the link and the text of the balloon.
A core name of nph-icon, at icon/size-md: light at rest, solid when active.
The page it leads to. Required unless disabled.
The current page: aria-current="page", sidebar/rail-background-active and the icon in sidebar/rail-foreground-active.
A whole number from zero up, read in the name of the link, after the label.
state/disabled-opacity, out of the Tab order, no balloon.
sidebarItemDocs.moreActionsText: tooltip turns on the nph-tooltip with the full name, on hover and focus: turn it on when the label can be cut. More actions is the icon-only nph-button, ghost and compact, with ellipsis-vertical, at the end of the line, on hover and focus; it opens an nph-dropdown-menu with the actions. It serves mouse and keyboard only: on touch it does not appear, so the same actions are on the destination page.
sidebarItemDocs.moreActionsCaption: A cut label with its balloon, and an item with more actions. Move the mouse over them, or press Tab.
relations: The pieces live inside nph-sidebar, which decides the expanded or collapsed mode, the width and the switch of the item for the rail button. The item fills the width it receives.
A group opens its subitems right below it. A subitem with the right arrow says it leads to a list of options.
The balloon is nph-tooltip, more actions is nph-button with nph-dropdown-menu, and the counter uses the primary palette. Each piece keeps its own state and focus.

Space: space/control-padding between icon and label and sidebar/item-padding around the item; on the subitem, space/inline between label and arrow and top and bottom, and sidebar/item-padding on the sides.
anatomy: nph-icon at icon/size-md, in the color of the label; solid when active or in an open group.
One line in text/body-md, text/label-md when active or in an open group, with an ellipsis when it does not fit.

A pill with the number in text/label-sm, in sidebar/item-badge-background and sidebar/item-badge-foreground, icon/size-md high, space/inline on the sides, radius/full. Only on a link and on the rail button.
icon/size-sm: down in a closed group, up in an open group, right on a subitem with options.
The icon-only nph-button, ghost and compact, with ellipsis-vertical, at the end, on hover and focus.
nph-tooltip with the full name, on hover and focus.
sidebar/item-background-hover on hover; none at rest and when active. On the rail button, sidebar/rail-background-hover on hover and sidebar/rail-background-active when active.

Border color/primary and halo focus/halo around the line, in focus/border-radius-sidebar-item and focus/radius-sidebar-item; on the rail button, focus/border-radius-container and focus/radius-container.
accessibility: Semantics
The item and the subitem are links, with aria-current="page" on the current page; a group is a button with aria-expanded. Disabled, the link has no href, keeps role link and gains aria-disabled.
Accessible name

From the label. The counter number is read as text, inside the name of the link. On the rail button, the balloon text and the counter make the name, through aria-labelledby, so the name holds the number one sees (WCAG 2.5.3). The icon and the arrow are hidden from the screen reader. More actions has its own name, actions-label.
Keyboard
Tab reaches the line and then, when there is one, the more actions button. Enter follows the link; Enter and Space open and close a group.
Visible focus
Border color/primary and halo focus/halo around the whole line, as in nph-button. The border passes 3:1 against sidebar/panel-background.
Contrast
Label, number and icon pass 4.5:1 and 3:1 against the line background, in both modes; the number against sidebar/item-badge-background. Disabled is exempt.
Color is not the only signal
Active also switches the icon to solid and the label to text/label-md. An open group shows the arrow up. On the rail button, active also gains its background.
Touch target
The whole line: sidebar/item-height on the item, control/height-default on the subitem, sidebar/rail-button-size on the rail button. More actions is small and serves mouse and keyboard only.

paginationDocs.summary: The bar that takes the person from one page to another in a long list and shows where in the list they are.
paginationDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-pagination spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and icons, and P99 for the API. Five decisions wait for the design owner (D-1 to D-5 of DSA-54) and show here in their default.
paginationDocs.sourceFrame: Figma, page NPH — Pagination, documentation 1640:196, set 1640:194
paginationDocs.sourceStates: Figma, page 2888:87682 and ellipsis 2888:87798; task DSA-54, pending decisions D-1 and D-2
paginationDocs.sourceFields: Figma, go to page 2888:87805; nph-select and nph-input spec sheets
paginationDocs.description: Use nph-pagination below a list or table that does not fit on one screen. It splits the result; it does not replace the filter or the search. Load more and infinite scroll are not part of this piece.
whenToUse: With type numbered, below a common list or search result, when the person jumps between nearby pages.
With type simple or compact, in a narrow space: compact fits a card header, a side panel and a phone.
With type edges, with go to page, in a long list, when the person needs to reach the start, the end or a given page.
With type range, when the total of items matters more than the page number.
With type table, in the footer of a data table with many records.
whenNotToUse: To filter or search the list: pagination splits the result, it does not replace the filter or the search.
To load more or scroll without end: they are not part of this piece.
To move between the steps of a flow: pagination moves between pages of the same list.
api: numbered (default), simple, edges, range, compact or table: the Figma tipo. The Figma posição is not a property: it comes from page and the page count.
The current page, a whole number from 1, reflected. The piece changes it when the person moves. Above the count, the last page is drawn, with one warning.

paginationDocs.invalidText: A type outside the six, a page or count that is not a whole number, no page count, range or table without total-items and page-size, page-sizes outside table or without page-size, go to page outside edges, and an arrow or a position text without its text each emit one console.error in development. With no label or no page-label, the piece draws and warns once.
paginationDocs.typesCaption: numbered, simple, edges, range, compact and table, in the middle of the list.
types: Numbers, with Previous and Next written.
Arrows and the position text with the word page.
Numbers with first, previous, next and last.
Arrows and the range of items.
Arrows and the short position text.

paginationDocs.positionText: The position is not a property: it comes from page and the page count. At the start, first and previous are disabled; in the middle, every arrow is active and an ellipsis sits on both sides of the current page; at the end, next and last are disabled. The first and the last page are always shown, and above seven pages the numbers keep seven slots, so the bar keeps its width.
paginationDocs.positionCaption: Start, middle and end of a list of ten pages.
paginationDocs.statesText: The numbers and the arrows are native buttons painted with the pagination tokens, with the focus of the secondary nph-button and, on the icon-only arrows, the balloon of the icon-only button (D-1). The first and last arrows use arrow-left-to-line; the last one turns only its icon. Previous and next use the chevrons (D-3).
paginationDocs.statesCaption: At the start: the current page, and first and previous disabled. Move the mouse for hover and the balloon, and press Tab for the focus.
states: No background, the number in pagination/text-foreground and text/label-md (D-2).
pagination/item-background-active and the number in text/label-md-strong, with aria-current="page".
pagination/arrow-background with a pagination/arrow-border stroke inside; the icon light.
pagination/item-background-hover; the icon solid; the balloon after the wait.
pagination/disabled-opacity, in place, out of the Tab order, with no hover and no balloon.
Border focus/border and halo focus/halo outside the button, keyboard only; on an arrow, the balloon opens at once.
paginationDocs.fieldsTitle: Items per page and go to page
paginationDocs.fieldsText: In table, items per page is an nph-select in pagination/page-size-width with its visible label: changing it keeps the first item on screen. In edges, go to page is an nph-input in pagination/page-input-width beside the bar: Enter goes to the typed page, past the end to the last one.
paginationDocs.fieldsCaption: Items per page in table, and go to page in edges.
relations: Sits right below the nph-data-table or the list it paginates. The table controls the data; pagination only changes the page.
Uses nph-icon for the arrows and the ellipsis, nph-tooltip for the balloons, nph-select for items per page and nph-input for go to page.
Space between the numbers and between the arrows: pagination/item-gap. Between groups: pagination/group-gap. Between a label and its field: pagination/control-gap.
anatomy: Outline pagination/border in pagination/border-width, radius pagination/radius, padding pagination/padding-x and pagination/padding-y (D-5).
Previous and next; first and last in edges and table. pagination/arrow-background, stroke pagination/arrow-border, radius pagination/item-radius.
A number in pagination/item-size, radius pagination/item-radius, text pagination/text-foreground. The current one has pagination/item-background-active.
Marks the pages that are not shown. Takes no click.
Page 5 of 10, 5 of 10 or 101–125 of 250, in simple, compact, range and table (D-4).
A label and an nph-select in pagination/page-size-width, only in table.
accessibility: Semantics
A navigation named by label. Each number and arrow is a native button; the current page carries aria-current="page". The ellipsis is hidden and takes no click.
Accessible name
Each number is named by page-label. The icon-only arrows are named by their balloon text, announced once; in numbered, the written text names the arrow.
Keyboard
Tab walks the arrows, the numbers and the fields in reading order, skipping a disabled arrow; Enter and Space move. Reaching the first or last page by an arrow moves the focus to the current page.
Contrast
Number, text and icon in pagination/text-foreground pass 4.5:1 in both modes, also over the active and hover backgrounds; the arrow border passes 3:1.
Color is not the only signal
The current page also has the number in bold. The arrow without a destination is disabled and shows no balloon.
Touch target
Number and arrow are pagination/item-size wide and high. On a narrow screen, use compact instead of shrinking the buttons.
do: Show the first and the last page in numbered: the person understands the size of the list.
Disable the arrow without a destination instead of hiding it: the bar keeps its width.
Use in items per page the same value the table uses: the range matches the rows on screen.
dont: Do not hide the arrow without a destination: the bar jumps.
Do not mark the current page only with the color of the number: color alone is not a signal.
references: Figma DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0, page NPH — Pagination, documentation 1640:196, set 1640:194

chipDocs.summary: The small rounded piece that shows an applied filter, a value chosen in a field or a quick filter that the person checks and unchecks.
chipDocs.derivedText: In case of divergence, the canonical sources prevail: the nph-chip spec sheet, design.md for the tokens and icons, and P100 for the API. Five decisions wait for the design owner (D-1 to D-5 of DSA-57) and show here in their default: the counter drawn as a pill of its own, the avatar in the sm size, the cut label focusable with its balloon, the invalid X with the error pair, and the order icon, text, counter and X.
chipDocs.sourceFrame: Figma, page NPH — Chip, documentation 3077:2240, set 3076:1439, board 3077:807
chipDocs.sourceStates: Figma, documentation 3077:2240, tokens of each state; task DSA-57, pending decision D-4
chipDocs.sourceContent: Figma, documentation 3077:2240; task DSA-57, pending decisions D-1, D-2 and D-5
chipDocs.sourceLongText: Figma, documentation 3077:2240; task DSA-57, pending decision D-3
chipDocs.description: Use nph-chip for applied filters in nph-toolbar, for the values chosen inside a field and for quick filters that the person checks and unchecks. It does not replace nph-badge, which shows a system status with no action, nor nph-button, which runs an action.
whenToUse: With type removable, for a filter already applied or a value chosen that the person can take away.
With type selectable, for a quick filter that the person checks and unchecks; several can stay checked.
With a status severity, when the value of the filter is a status; the label says which.
With an icon, to recognize the type of the filter; with an avatar, when the value is a person; with a counter, to show how many items the option has before the click.
With size compact in the toolbar, the table and the field; with size default on a selectable chip inside a form.
whenNotToUse: For a system status with no action: use nph-badge.
To run an action, such as delete the selected: use nph-button.
In a line of chips that scrolls sideways: let the chips wrap.
api: removable (default) or selectable: the Figma tipo. In removable the X takes the value away and the body has no action; in selectable the whole chip is a toggle button.
default, success, warning, error, info or help: the Figma cor. A status color exists only on a removable chip with text content.
compact (default) or default: the Figma tamanho. The target of the X is the same in both.
The label, already localized, in one line. Cut with an ellipsis at the maximum width, with the whole text in a balloon. Without text, the piece draws nothing and emits no error.
A core name of nph-icon, before the text. At most one of icon, avatar and counter.
Draws an nph-avatar before the text, only in removable. avatar-src is the photo; without it, the avatar draws the person icon.
A whole number from zero up, after the text, only in selectable.
The word the X says before the text, such as Remove filter, so the X reads Remove filter Status: Waiting. Required while the X shows on a removable chip.
The checked selectable chip, which shows the X as a mark: the click belongs to the whole chip. Changing it from code fires nothing.
The removable states marcado, somente leitura and inválido, in the default severity and one at a time. Read only has no X.
The whole chip at reduced opacity, out of the Tab order, with no click and no balloon. It wins over the other states, with no error.
Fired only when the person presses the X of a removable chip, with detail text; bubbles and is composed. The chip does not remove itself.
Fired only when the person toggles a selectable chip, with detail selected, after selected changed; bubbles and is composed.
chipDocs.invalidText: A type, a severity or a size outside the lists, an icon outside the core, more than one of icon, avatar and counter, a counter on a removable chip, an avatar or a status severity on a selectable chip, a state in a status severity or on a selectable chip, a status severity with an icon or an avatar, and a removable chip with an X and no remove-label each emit one console.error in development. A chip with no text draws nothing and emits no error.
chipDocs.usageTag: The tag of the piece. It has no slot: the text and every other content come as attributes.
chipDocs.usageImport: Registers the component with its styles. The generated token CSS is imported on its own.
chipDocs.typesCaption: removable and selectable, in the default severity and size.
types: An applied filter or a chosen value that the person can take away. The X takes the value away and fires nph-remove; the body has no action.
A quick filter that the person checks and unchecks with one click. The whole chip is a toggle button with aria-pressed, and fires nph-selected-change.
chipDocs.severitiesText: The default severity is the color of the chip. The status colors apply to a removable chip with text: the value of the filter is a status, and the label says which. Each color has its own border, background and label; the X stays in the foreground color.
chipDocs.severitiesCaption: default, success, warning, error, info and help.
severities: chip/<status>-background, border chip/<status>-border and label chip/<status>-foreground, with <status> as the severity.
chipDocs.sizesText: Compact in the toolbar, the table and the field; default on a selectable chip inside a form. The X has the same target, chip/remove-size, in both.
chipDocs.statesText: marked, readonly and invalid are attributes of a removable chip, one at a time, in the default severity. selected belongs to a selectable chip. disabled wins over the others. Hover, focus and active are interaction states: move the mouse over the X or the chip and press Tab to see them.
chipDocs.statesCaption: Removable: default, marked, read only, invalid and disabled. Selectable: default, selected and disabled.
states: chip/background, border chip/border, label chip/foreground. Read only has no X.
chip/background-hover; the focus ring (focus/border and focus/halo) around the whole chip: the last chip of a field, ready to leave.
The X on chip/remove-background-hover; in a status color, chip/<status>-remove-background-hover.
Border focus/border and halo focus/halo around the X; in a status color, chip/<status>-focus-border and chip/<status>-focus-halo.
chip/invalid-background, border chip/invalid-border, text chip/invalid-foreground; the X takes the error pair on hover and focus (D-4).
chip/background, border chip/border, label chip/foreground, counter chip/counter-background.
chip/background-hover and the counter on chip/counter-background-hover, so the pill does not disappear.
Border focus/border and halo focus/halo around the whole chip.
chip/background-selected, label chip/foreground-selected, no border and the X shown as a mark. On hover, chip/background-selected-hover.
chip/background-disabled, no border, at state/disabled-opacity; out of the Tab order, with no click and no balloon. The selected chip keeps its full background.
chipDocs.contentText: The Figma conteúdo is not a property. An icon helps to recognize the type of the filter; an avatar, when the value is a person (removable only); a counter, to show how many items the option has before the click (selectable only). At most one of them, in the order icon, text, counter and X (D-5).
chipDocs.contentCaption: Text, icon and avatar on a removable chip; text, icon and counter on a selectable one.
content: nph-icon at icon/size-sm, before the text, decorative. Start padding chip/padding-start-icon.
nph-avatar in the sm size (D-2), before the text, decorative. Start padding chip/padding-start-avatar.
A pill of its own after the text, on chip/counter-background, with the number in chip/counter-foreground and text/label-sm (D-1). End padding chip/padding-end-counter.
chipDocs.longTextText: The label is one line. It is cut with an ellipsis at chip/max-width, and the whole text shows in a balloon on hover and on keyboard focus. To give the balloon a target, the cut label itself takes the focus (D-3); a label that is not cut takes no focus and has no balloon, and a disabled chip has none.
chipDocs.longTextCaption: A long label on a removable and on a selectable chip.
relations: In nph-toolbar, the applied filters sit in a line below the bar, and Clear filters (nph-button secondary, ghost, compact) comes after the last chip.
Inside a field, each chosen value becomes a removable chip; the field controls the border, the focus of the group and the error message.
Uses nph-icon, nph-avatar and nph-tooltip inside. The counter is drawn by the chip itself (D-1).
nph-badge shows a status with no action; the chip always has an action: remove or toggle.
Space between chips: space/inline. When there is no room, the chips wrap to the next line.
anatomy: chip/background, radius chip/radius, height chip/height-compact or chip/height-default, maximum width chip/max-width. A border chip/border-width inside, in the color of the severity; none on the selected and disabled chip; chip/invalid-border on the invalid one.
Optional, before the text. Decorative: the click belongs to the chip.
Text in text/label-md, color chip/foreground, one line, cut with an ellipsis at the maximum width.
Optional, selectable only: a pill with chip/counter-background and chip/counter-foreground, and chip/counter-padding-y and chip/counter-padding-x inside.
The X button, with target chip/remove-size and radius chip/remove-radius. Background chip/remove-background-hover on hover, focus and active.
accessibility: Contrast

Text and X pass 4.5:1 over the chip background in every state, in light and dark. The border marks the edge of the chip against the page; it does not need 3:1, because the text already identifies the piece.
Visible focus
Border focus/border with halo focus/halo around the chip, on a selectable one, or around the X, on a removable one. In a status chip, the ring of the X follows the status color.
Color
Color is never the only signal: the selected chip shows the X and the full background; the status is written in the label; the invalid chip has a red border and a message below the field.
Touch target
The X has the target chip/remove-size in both sizes.
Accessible name

The X is a native button named by remove-label and the text, such as Remove filter Status: Waiting. Icon and avatar are hidden from the screen reader. A selectable chip is a toggle button with aria-pressed.
Keyboard
Tab reaches the X of a removable chip and the whole selectable chip, and skips a disabled one; Enter and Space press the X or toggle the chip. A cut label also takes the focus, so its balloon opens.
Disabled and read only
Disabled takes no focus and no click. Read only shows the value without the X. Marked is the last chip of the field, ready to leave.
do: Use removable for an applied filter: the X shows how to undo it.
Show the X on the selected chip: the state does not depend on color alone.
Write a short label, such as Field: value: the person understands the filter without opening anything.
Let the chips wrap: all stay visible and in reading order.
dont: Do not use a chip for a system status with no action: use nph-badge.
Do not use a chip to run an action: use nph-button.
Do not put the line of chips in a horizontal scroll: let it wrap.
references: Figma DS-IA-NEPHOS 5.0, page NPH — Chip, documentation 3077:2240, set 3076:1439, board 3077:807
